title: NPM: Playwright does not work
body: I'm trying to use Playwright through Deno's new NPM compatibility layer. After installing the required Chromium binary with `deno run --unstable --allow-all npm:playwright install`, running my script with `deno run --unstable --allow-all main.ts` launches Chromium but then fails with `browserType.launch: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on')`. The script imports `chromium` from `npm:playwright`, launches it, opens a page, visits `http://example.com`, and closes the browser.

symptoms_visible: After I install Playwright's Chromium binary and rerun the script, Chromium is launched but `chromium.launch()` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on')`.
N0.label: N0 Playwright launch failure reported

symptoms_visible: In the debugger, Playwright reaches its pipe transport setup after launching Chromium, but entries 3 and 4 of the child process's `stdio` array are undefined.
N1.label: N1 missing Playwright transport pipes observed

symptoms_visible: When I launch Chromium manually and connect with `connectOverCDP`, the server returns `101 Switching Protocols`, but Playwright treats it as an unexpected response and the WebSocket closes before any messages are sent.
N2_x.label: N2_x manual CDP WebSocket workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: With Playwright's WebSocket launch mode, the browser starts and connects, but navigating a page closes the browser and reports `Invalid WebSocket frame: RSV2 and RSV3 must be clear`.
N3_x.label: N3_x Playwright WebSocket launch workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: Other affected users can now install Playwright, launch browsers, and run tests successfully with current Deno builds on macOS and Linux; I, the original reporter, have not personally retested the final build, and equivalent Windows support has not been confirmed.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal fix available and verified by other affected users

question_patterns: Can you pause on the exception with `--inspect-brk` and report the values Playwright passes to `PipeTransport`?
What does the launched child process's `stdio` array contain when Playwright constructs its browser transport?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the reproduction with `--inspect-brk` and examined the call stack. At Playwright's `new PipeTransport(stdio[3], stdio[4])` call, both `stdio[3]` and `stdio[4]` are undefined. I attached a debugger screenshot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both `stdio[3]` and `stdio[4]` are valid streams; the exception occurs later while parsing a browser protocol message.
The same two entries are undefined on Linux instead of macOS.

edges.comment: From c0-c2. The debugger run and screenshot came from participant1 on an affected macOS system and are folded into the simulated user side. The raw observation is that stdio entries 3 and 4 are undefined; concluding that Deno lacks the required extra-pipe support remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Avoid Playwright's missing pipe transport by launching Chromium separately with a remote debugging port and connecting through `chromium.connectOverCDP()` over WebSocket.
solution.concrete_example: Replace Chromium's `--remote-debugging-pipe` argument with `--remote-debugging-port=0`, copy the printed DevTools WebSocket address, and pass it to `chromium.connectOverCDP()`.

edges.comment: Reporter c3-c6 tried the WebSocket/CDP route to bypass the unavailable pipes. The handshake returned HTTP 101, but Deno's Node HTTP/WebSocket compatibility path emitted an unexpected-response event and sent no WebSocket messages, so this was not a working resolution at that point.

solution.intent: Use Playwright's browser-server WebSocket mode so Playwright starts Chromium and returns an endpoint without manual command copying.
solution.concrete_example: Start Chromium with `chromium.launchServer({ useWebSocket: true })`, obtain `browserServer.wsEndpoint()`, and connect with `chromium.connect(wsEndpoint)`.

edges.comment: Reporter c13 proposed launchServer/connect as a less manual route; participant6 c14 tested the undocumented useWebSocket option. These affected-user reports are folded together. The browser connected but closed during navigation with an invalid WebSocket-frame error, so it was still not a reliable fix.

solution.intent: Fix Deno's Node child-process compatibility by supporting the extra inherited stdio pipes Playwright uses for Chromium's protocol transport, then have affected users verify Playwright on a build containing that support.
solution.concrete_example: Extend subprocess spawning on macOS and Linux so a native Chromium child can inherit Playwright's additional pipes at file descriptors 3 and 4. Then rerun the original `chromium.launch()` example and Playwright tests on a current build; do not claim equivalent Windows support until its separate process-spawning work is implemented and verified.
solution.inference_hint: The debugger only establishes that Playwright receives undefined values for stdio entries 3 and 4. Maintainers concluded that Deno's child-process implementation lacked support for Playwright's additional inherited pipes and that the general raw-file-descriptor problem could be sidestepped because Chromium is a native child process. That causal interpretation is engineer inference, not user-provided output.

edges.comment: Opening chain resolution from c25-c26 and c38-c43. Maintainers implemented extra stdio-pipe support for native child processes on macOS and Linux. Later affected users confirmed successful Playwright installation, browser launching, and tests on those platforms. The original reporter did not return to verify the final build, and c30-c35/c45 establish that Windows remained separate work; the terminal therefore does not claim reporter-perceived resolution. Later test-runner configuration and UI-loader issues are independent sub-problems and are not chained onto the opening launch failure.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Deno's Node child-process compatibility layer did not provide the additional inherited stdio pipes at file descriptors 3 and 4 that Playwright uses to communicate with the native Chromium child process.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the debugger observation that `stdio[3]` and `stdio[4]` were undefined even though Chromium had launched.

The technical fix must add the extra child-process pipes needed by Playwright's pipe transport; manually launching Chromium and relying on the historical WebSocket workarounds must not be presented as the final resolution because those routes failed in the case.
Must scope the established support to macOS and Linux and avoid claiming that the same process-spawning support was established for Windows.

Must ask for verification on a build containing the extra-pipe support before declaring the original reporter's system resolved; other affected users verified macOS and Linux, but the original reporter did not report a final retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical application developer evaluating Deno as an embeddable JavaScript runtime; comfortable with TypeScript, Rust integration, browser debugging, HTTP/WebSocket traces, proxies, and detailed reproduction work, but unfamiliar with Deno's internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Methodical, cooperative, and unusually detailed. Documents exact commands, scripts, logs, debugger observations, and failed experiments, and clearly distinguishes tentative theories from reproduced behavior.
